_note: Data-claim manifest — the single source of truth for the book's governed data cross-references. One entry per grounded datum. A `[data: <slug>]` marker in the prose resolves against this file to a footnote-style cross-ref into the chapter that reports the number (fail-loud on an unknown slug, like an unknown {{token}}). Fields: `source` = the chapter slug (a book/<slug>.html page) that reports the datum; `anchor` = the {#heading-id} on that chapter's reporting section; `holds` = the load-bearing numbers/units that MUST still appear in the source (the check_data_claims lint compares digit-sequences+units under a loose match, so a spelling change is fine but a real number change fails); `status` = final | preliminary | partial; `gloss` = a one-line description of the datum. Regenerate the anchors + this file together when a source section moves. Queryable via `catalog.py data-claims`.

refactor-cost.gloss: A cross-format migration touched fifty-eight files and rewrote five thousand lines in about five hours of agent time — refactoring became an afternoon's work.

nearly-free.gloss: The per-document remediation cost cascade — do-it-yourself professor cost vs. external-vendor quote vs. the tool's per-deck processing cost — showing high-quality remediation nearly for free.

velocity.gloss: The velocity curve: commits per week across the project's history, rising as the fleet acquired capability then dipping during hardening.

mbse-nav-token.gloss: A controlled A/B pilot of MBSE navigation guidance (N=4 modeled tasks): tokens-to-answer with guidance ON vs. OFF, saving -20% / -12% / -82% / -50%, median ~-35%, zero accuracy loss.
